content: Spouses married August 1966 under community property, purchased property in Ragusa during marriage. Following divorce January 2008 (final), wife sought division and compensation for husband's exclusive use since October 2004. Husband agreed to division with assignment but contested compensation, citing April 2003 court order assigning marital home to him, arguing exclusive possession legitimate. He counterclaimed reimbursement under Article 192 for mortgage payments (€30,507.53) and property improvements (€26,127.27). Articles 177, 192, 194, 1114 Italian Civil Code govern community property purchases, personal funds reimbursement, equal division principle, and convenient divisibility. The issues concerned compensation for exclusive occupation where assignment ordered by separation proceedings, and reimbursement rights for alleged personal fund expenditures. Court-appointed expert determined property value €142,000 total but deemed in-kind division uneconomical: excellent repair state and considerable division costs (€48,000) make division inadvisable. Convenient divisibility requires structurally feasible portions capable of independent enjoyment without excessive costs, and no significant depreciation. Property assigned to husband already in possession; wife receives compensation for her 50% share (€71,000) plus interest. Compensation for occupation rejected: husband took possession February 2005 pursuant to April 2003 court order confirmed by Court of Appeal April 2004. Assignment provided legitimate right to reside—exclusive possession of common property lawful where authorized by court order absent appeal against assignment order. Counterclaim for mortgage/improvement reimbursement rejected: Article 192(III) grants reimbursement for personal sums used for joint investments, but inapplicable to purchase payments falling under Article 177(a) where mandatory equal division applies regardless of contribution extent per Article 194(I). Renovation expense reimbursement rejected: possessor must consult/notify other participant before incurring expenses; expenses partly incurred during marriage (benefiting both) and partly post-2005 (benefiting only husband exclusively enjoying property). Costs compensated given mutual defeat; expert costs borne equally.
